findings.title: Uses queue.Queue.shutdown/queue.ShutDown, which require Python 3.13+
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` and the worker catches `queue.ShutDown`. Both APIs were added in Python 3.13. On older supported runtimes the shutdown path raises AttributeError for every queue and workers blocked in `get()` are never released; the worker exception handler also cannot resolve `queue.ShutDown`, so an unexpected processing exception can kill the worker thread. This makes the new consumer unable to shut down correctly unless the whole repository is already on Python 3.13.

findings.title: Broad submit exception handler commits offsets for messages that were never enqueued
findings.body: If `grouping_fn(result)` raises, or if `queue_pool.submit` fails (for example `work_queue.put` raises `ShutDown` during shutdown), the `except Exception` block calls `add_offset` plus `complete_offset` for the message. The commit thread then sees the offset as complete and commits past it even though the message was never processed or even queued. Only an intentional decode failure returning `None` should be skipped; unexpected failures must propagate, retry, or go to a DLQ rather than silently advancing the Kafka offset.

findings.title: Worker marks an offset complete even when result processing raised
findings.body: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches `Exception` from `result_processor`, logs it, and then unconditionally calls `complete_offset` in `finally`. Any exception that escapes processing (a bug, tracing failure, unexpected DB error, etc.) therefore makes the offset committable and permanently skips that message. This contradicts the class contract that offsets are only committed after successful processing and turns transient failures into silent data loss.

findings.title: Commit callback is invoked from a background thread concurrently with the stream processor
findings.body: `_commit_loop` runs on its own thread and calls the arroyo `Commit` callback, which ultimately commits the Kafka consumer used by the main `StreamProcessor` polling thread. The Confluent Kafka consumer and arroyo commit path are not thread-safe, and existing strategies only call `commit` from the processing thread. This can race with `poll`/rebalance and cause undefined behavior, failed commits, or duplicate processing. Commit requests should be handed back to the processing thread or otherwise serialized.

findings.title: Work queues are unbounded, so the strategy has no backpressure
findings.body: `queue.Queue()` is created with the default `maxsize=0`, so `put()` never blocks. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` continues accepting messages as fast as Kafka delivers them even if one or more queues cannot keep up; each queued `WorkItem` retains both the decoded result and the full original `Message`. A single slow subscription can therefore grow memory without bound and eventually OOM the consumer. The class docstring claiming `Natural backpressure when queues fill up` is false unless a bounded queue and blocking submission are added.

findings.title: Shutdown stops workers before draining queued work
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets every worker's `shutdown` flag before shutting down the queues. Workers check that flag only at the top of the loop, so a worker that is processing an item exits immediately afterwards even if more items remain in its queue. The existing `wait_until_empty` helper is never used. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close`/`join` therefore can abandon messages that were already accepted by `submit`, causing avoidable reprocessing on restart and making the `graceful shutdown` behavior misleading. Shutdown should stop accepting new work, drain queued and in-flight items, and only then stop workers.

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts no commit even though failed offsets are marked complete
findings.body: The test patches `result_processor.__call__` to raise for offset 100 and succeed for offset 101. In the implementation, the worker catches the exception and `finally` calls `complete_offset`, so both offsets become committable and the commit loop will normally commit past offset 100. The assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` can only pass if the 1-second commit thread happens not to run during the 0.2-second sleep, so the test is timing-dependent and also does not encode the intended error semantics. It should explicitly define whether failed messages are retried, sent to a DLQ, or committed, and assert that contract deterministically.

findings.title: Stats test races with live queue workers
findings.body: `test_stats_reporting` submits ten items to a live pool and immediately asserts `stats['total_items'] > 0`. The three worker threads can dequeue and process all ten items before `get_stats()` is called, making `total_items` zero and causing an intermittent failure. The test should synchronize with the workers (for example by pausing them or using a barrier) instead of assuming queue depth remains non-zero after submission.
